prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

Public finances and economy
- Allow modest annual increases in public spending while reducing deficit and debt as a share of income; balance current spending over the medium term.
- Prioritise infrastructure investment, productivity, and job creation; create a sovereign wealth/energy fund when conditions allow.
- Raise revenues via restoring the 50p top income tax rate, a bankers’ bonus tax, higher bank levy, a mansion tax, abolishing non-dom status, tackling avoidance, reviewing pension tax relief, and reversing the married couples’ allowance.
- Seed-fund a national business development bank; expand export finance; strengthen late-payment protections; raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019–20; provide stability for Annual Investment Allowance.
- Cut and devolve Air Passenger Duty, consider a VAT cut for hospitality, and expand support for creative industries (including fairer BBC spend, games sector incentives).
- Reintroduce a post‑study work visa; City Deals for all cities; increase northern UK infrastructure focus; connect Scotland to HS2; expand broadband/4G with a telecoms Universal Service Obligation.
- Support a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes annually and further housebuilding in Scotland.

Work, pay and equality
- Increase the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the living wage; equal pay audits for large firms; strengthen maternity discrimination laws; remove VAT on sanitary products.
- Modernise union balloting (including secure online voting); restore 90‑day consultation for large redundancies; increase employee representation on boards; address exploitative zero‑hour contracts.

Welfare and pensions
- Abolish the Bedroom Tax; halt and review Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA to PIP change; raise the work allowance by 20%; uprate benefits at least by cost of living.
- Increase Carer’s Allowance to match Jobseeker’s Allowance; review sanctions/conditionality; protect Savings Credit; oppose restricting housing benefit for 18–21s; disregard war disablement pensions in means tests.
- Support a single‑tier pension at £160/week with the triple lock; review state pension age rise to 67; retain winter fuel allowance; tackle pension charges.

Health, education and childcare
- Increase UK health spending (yielding about £2bn extra for Scotland by 2020–21); protect the NHS from privatisation; expand mental health funding; integrate health and social care; fund delayed discharges and new medicines.
- Expand free childcare to 30 hours/week for 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; maintain free university tuition; deliver 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships; expand Educational Maintenance Allowance.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Fund ECO from general taxation; require suppliers to pass through wholesale price cuts; ensure prepayment parity; earlier winter fuel payments for off‑grid pensioners.
- Support a fracking moratorium; oppose renewal of the UK nuclear deterrent.
- Match ambitious carbon‑reduction targets; prioritise offshore wind, sustain onshore wind, support hydro, CCS, storage, island interconnectors, and transmission charging reform; expand community energy and renewable heat.

Rural, postal, and food policy
- Protect Royal Mail’s Universal Service Obligation, retain a 30% public stake, and pursue return to public ownership over time.
- Secure fair CAP convergence funding; simplify CAP; implement discard ban practicably; return seabed leasing net income to coastal communities; devolve food levies; promote food and drink, including whisky duty reform.

Justice, policing, data
- Retain 1,000 additional police officers; keep court fines revenue in Scotland; seek VAT exemption for police and fire services.
- Oppose blanket data retention; support targeted, overseen measures against extremism.
- Devolve regulation of fixed‑odds betting terminals and payday lending.

Governance and rights
- Strengthen MP recall; adopt Single Transferable Vote; replace the House of Lords with an elected chamber; extend voting to 16–17‑year‑olds; refine lobbying rules while easing limits on charity campaigning.
- Maintain the Human Rights Act and ECHR commitments; advance gender balance on public boards; support a Race Committee; review immigration detention; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy.

EU, trade, foreign and defence
- Support continued EU membership with a “double‑majority” requirement for any UK exit; expand devolved roles in EU decision‑making; exempt public services from TTIP; retain European Arrest Warrant.
- Maintain 0.7% GNI for international development; exclude defence spend from aid; audit developing‑country debt; require parliamentary approval for military action; support a two‑state solution in the Middle East.
- Refocus defence on northern/Arctic needs; procure maritime patrol aircraft and patrol vessels in Scotland; increase regional transparency in defence spend; build Type 26 frigates and refit carriers in Scotland; improve support for service personnel and families.

Devolution
- Implement the Smith Commission swiftly and fully, without effective vetoes.
- Seek further devolution toward full financial responsibility; prioritise employment policy (including minimum wage), welfare, business taxes, National Insurance, equality, and broadcasting during transition; keep Barnett Formula until full responsibility is achieved.

TEXT_F:
Summary of the 2015 manifesto (policy commitments only)

Fiscal and tax
- No new spending funded by additional borrowing; cut the deficit every year; aim for a current-budget surplus and falling national debt; independent OBR audits of manifestos; cap structural social security spending.
- Restore the 50p top income tax rate; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Allowance; no rises in basic/higher Income Tax, National Insurance or VAT; abolish non‑dom status; close loopholes; public beneficial-ownership registers; HMRC culture review.
- Restrict Winter Fuel Payments to the richest 5% of pensioners; cap child benefit rises for two years; all Lloyds/RBS sale proceeds to debt reduction.

Economy, business and infrastructure
- National Infrastructure Commission; proceed with HS2, improve northern rail, invest in roads/cycling; swift airport-capacity decision.
- Long-term science and innovation framework; lead in low‑carbon tech; decarbonise electricity by 2030; strengthen Green Investment Bank; create an Energy Security Board; robust fracking regime; offshore oil/gas strategy.
- Nationwide affordable high‑speed broadband and wider mobile coverage; digital inclusion.
- Corporate-governance reforms: empower long‑term investors; tighten takeover rules; employee voice on pay; disclose pay votes.
- Support co‑ops/mutuals; retain 30% of Royal Mail.
- British Investment Bank and regional banks; increase banking competition; levy on payday lenders; cut and freeze small business rates; tackle late payments.

Work, skills and young people
- Raise National Minimum Wage to >£8 by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and first‑year tax rebates; listed firms to report LW status.
- Ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; right to a regular contract after 12 weeks; end agency undercutting; abolish employment‑tribunal fees system.
- Cut tuition fees to £6,000; paid jobs guarantee for long‑term unemployed (funded by a bank bonus tax); apprenticeship guarantee for qualified school leavers; require apprenticeships in major public contracts; shift provision to Level 3+, 2+ years; introduce Technical Degrees; Youth Allowance tied to training.

Consumer markets, energy and transport
- Freeze energy bills to 2017; stronger regulator (including licence removal); separate generation/supply in large firms; simplify tariffs; energy‑efficiency loans; upgrade low‑income homes; minimum standards in private rentals.
- Water: national affordability scheme; stronger regulator powers.
- Rail: franchising reform with a public operator option; National Rail body; fare freeze next year, stricter caps, legal right to the cheapest ticket; devolved bus powers and smart ticketing.

Health and social care
- 20,000 nurses, 8,000 GPs, 3,000 midwives (funded by a mansion tax, tobacco levy, anti‑avoidance); 48‑hour GP appointments; one‑week cancer tests by 2020.
- Repeal competition regime; cap profits for private clinical providers; integrate physical, mental and social care with personal care plans and a single coordinator.
- Mental‑health parity; target 28‑day access to talking therapies; expand school‑based support; staff training on mental health.
- Public health: action on obesity and problem alcohol; nutrient limits in foods marketed to children.
- Social care: end 15‑minute visits; year‑of‑care budgets; recruit 5,000 home‑care workers; identify and support carers.

Education
- Protect the whole education budget; introduce a Technical Baccalaureate; create Institutes of Technical Education; English/Maths to 18; work experience 14–16; independent careers advice.
- Require qualified teachers; Master Teacher status and ongoing CPD; School Leadership Institute.
- Local Directors of School Standards; cap infant classes at 30; end the Free Schools programme; require private–state school partnerships for business‑rate relief; compulsory age‑appropriate SRE; tackle bullying.

Families, housing and welfare
- Expand free childcare for 3–4s from 15 to 25 hours for working parents; guaranteed wraparound childcare via primary schools; double paternity leave and raise pay; strengthen Sure Start.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; priority for local first‑time buyers; Future Homes Fund; land transparency; “use it or lose it” powers; back small/public builders; reform council housing finance; higher council tax on long‑term empty homes; garden cities.
- Private renting: three‑year tenancies as the norm, ceilings on rent rises, ban letting fees, national landlord register; reduce homelessness.
- Keep the benefit cap (review local variation); pause/review Universal Credit; higher contributory JSA; abolish the Bedroom Tax; reform the Work Capability Assessment; tailored disability employment support.

Immigration
- Recruit 1,000 extra border staff; full exit checks; tighten short‑term student visas; retain cap on non‑EU workers; curb exploitative recruitment; require English for public‑facing roles; two‑year wait for in‑work benefits for new EU arrivals; end indefinite detention (with protections); uphold refugee obligations.

Policing, justice and safety
- Protect neighbourhood policing (abolish PCCs, mandate force collaboration, end firearms‑licence subsidy); safeguard 10,000 officers; Local Policing Commitment; new Police Standards Authority; chartered officers; improve diversity.
- Payback orders for low‑level offences; stronger protections for public‑facing staff; youth‑justice pilots; integrate drug treatment; ban legal highs; new child‑protection powers/unit; prisons measured on rehabilitation; chartered prison officers; Victims’ Law.
- Violence against women and girls: bill, commissioner, stable refuge funding; tighter gun/DNA rules; wider legal aid access.

Extremism and hate crime
- Stronger terror controls; mandatory deradicalisation for Syria returnees; update powers with stronger oversight; overhaul Prevent; tougher hate‑crime laws.

Culture, sport, environment
- Universal creative‑education entitlement; rebalance arts funding; maintain free national‑museum entry; increase creative‑industry apprenticeships; fan representation on football boards; ensure 5% of Premier League TV income to grassroots.
- Climate adaptation programme; prioritise flood prevention; stronger local air‑quality powers; keep forests public; strengthen animal‑welfare laws; rural food/farm/fisheries strategy; expand supermarket watchdog.

Governance, devolution, rights and media
- People‑led Constitutional Convention; replace Lords with an elected Senate of Nations and Regions; English Devolution Act (£30bn, wider local powers, retain growth in business rates); local Public Accounts Committees; community powers over high streets (payday lenders/FOBTs).
- Implement further devolution for Scotland and Wales with fair funding; all‑Wales policing plan; support Northern Ireland agreements.
- Votes at 16–17; boost voter registration; cap party donations; repeal the Lobbying Act; statutory lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies.
- Gender pay‑gap reporting; stronger maternity‑discrimination law; race‑equality strategy; advance LGBT rights; protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR; extend FOI; repair judicial review.
- Media: modernise plurality rules; implement Leveson; support BBC value for money; keep Channel 4 public.

Europe, defence, foreign policy and development
- Remain engaged in NATO/EU; reform the EU (single market focus, protect non‑Euro members, red‑card for national parliaments, tighter migration/benefit rules); no power transfers without an in/out referendum.
- Strategic Defence and Security Review in year one; strengthen the Armed Forces Covenant (Veterans’ Register, anti‑discrimination, NHS Constitution); procurement reform; cyber‑security charter/reporting; maintain a minimum, credible independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Clear tests for military action; counter ISIL with allies; support a two‑state solution; sustain support for Afghanistan; Asia taskforce; envoys for religious freedom and international LGBT rights.
- Lead on Paris climate goals (net‑zero in the second half of the century).
- Maintain 0.7% aid; focus on the poorest and fragile states; Centre for Universal Health Coverage; reshape UN humanitarian system; extend tax‑information sharing to developing countries; tackle corruption and unethical supply chains.
